predecessors.name: Silla
predecessors.text: Silla after the conquest of Baekje and of Goguryeo south of the Taedong River

successors.name: Goryeo
successors.text: Silla's rump, the Gyeongsang region round Gyeongju

ledger.x: 682: Silla appears as 'Unified Silla' on the map.

682: Tamna, a tributary of Silla since 662, stays so ('Tributary state of Silla (662-925)', Tamna infobox); the relation began in the Silla dossier and is restated here because the dossier changes in 682.
901: Kung Ye proclaims Later Goguryeo at Kaesong.
c.905: Silla loses the centre and north to Kung Ye.
c.905: the northern edge of Cliopatria's outline passes to nobody.
925: the end of Tamna's tributary status to Silla ('Tributary state of Silla (662-925)', Tamna infobox); Goryeo's lordship over the island starts in 938.

wars.name: Tang-Balhae War
wars.outcome: Balhae raided Dengzhou in 732; Xuanzong ordered a Tang-Silla attack in 733 that was repelled (snow); Silla attacked Balhae without success in 734; Balhae made peace with Tang in 737.

wars.name: Later Three Kingdoms
wars.outcome: Silla lost the south-west to Later Baekje (892) and the centre and north to Kung Ye (c.905); Gyeongsun submitted to Goryeo in 935 and Later Baekje fell in 936.

wars.name: Later Baekje's sack of Gyeongju
wars.outcome: Kyŏn Hwŏn killed King Gyeongae and put Gyeongsun on the throne; Taejo was beaten near Daegu.

certainty.note: The northern line 'from the mouth of the Taedong River in the west to the East Korea Bay' was recognised by Tang in 736 (Silla-Tang War page), but no survey or treaty fixes it; the frontier with Balhae is approximate.
The fronts with Later Baekje and Kung Ye move year by year without a stated line.
